post.summary: Stop one agent turn (session owner only)
post.description: Records the stop request where every worker can see it. The turn starts no further model or tool call, the call running is cut, and the turn ends with a `stopped` event listing the writes already made. Idempotent: a repeat, or a call after the turn ended, answers 200 with the turn's state (`stopping`, `stopped` or `ended`).

post.summary: Retry a failed or stopped run as a new run (session owner only)
post.description: Only the chat's newest run, and only when it failed, was stopped or is stuck running (409 otherwise; a stuck one is stopped first). Starts a new run on the same plan whose task is told what failed and says why, then the failed step runs again and the run goes on. Returns the new run. activity.description: Optional manual-edit activity turn (round-26 §3.3): when present the save appends ONE `changed:true` transcript row for this manual/design edit — `{label, icon, scopes, change, client_activity_id}` the FE already computes — so the ghost becomes a real, seq-ordered, reload-durable timeline turn (with `version_before`/`version_after` from this save). The FE coalesces its own bursts before sending: one persist = one row. Omit for a save that shouldn't add a timeline turn.

prefer.description: When the head moved past `base_sequence` and both sides changed the same thing: settle it this way (the editor's 'Use mine' / 'Keep theirs') instead of answering 409. Everything else still merges.

base_canvas.description: The canvas this edit was made on top of, when that is NOT the stored version at `base_sequence`: after a `merged` save the editor still holds what it sent, without the colleague's change. Sent with `base_sequence` = that merged save's sequence; the save is then merged from this canvas, so the editor's own earlier save is never read as a colleague's.

loaded_sequence.description: With `base_canvas`: the version the editor's model was loaded at. Only names who changed things since (in a 409 or `merged_moves`); the merge itself runs from `base_canvas`.

prefer_for_head.description: With `prefer`: the head sequence of the 409 being answered. The choice applies only while the head is still there — if a colleague saved again since, the person is asked afresh instead of their answer overwriting a change they never saw.

accepts_merge.description: The client adopts a `merged` answer (it keeps the merged head before its next full-canvas save). Only such a client's stale save is merged; any other keeps the 409, since writing its un-merged model next would revert the colleague's change without a conflict.

merged.description: True when the head had moved past `base_sequence` and this save was merged onto it (a colleague's changes are in the new head too): the client must adopt the head before sending its next full canvas.

merged_moves.description: Who and what this save was merged with

recomposed.description: True when a content page's structure `type` changed vs the stored head and its architect tiles were re-picked for the new archetype (Design → Structure). False for an ordinary save.

changed_tiles.description: How many architect tiles entered or left the composition across the recomposed pages. 0 with `recomposed=True` is a legitimate tie (the new archetype re-picks the same charts for this data → 'layout already fits'); >0 drives the 'N charts updated' signal.

seeded_pages.description: Ids of brand-new EMPTY authored pages this save auto-seeded with a starter composition (the '+ add page' affordance lands pages via this PUT with no chat turn, so an authored page would otherwise bake to an empty tab). Non-empty means the persisted head now differs from what the client PUT — the client should refetch the draft canvas (GET /{id}/canvas) to pick up the seeded tiles.

format_floor.description: What the format-change floor added when this save changed the canvas `style` — the structure the new style needs that a switched board never received (it lives on the create path alone). Null for an ordinary save and for a switch that found nothing to fill. Non-null means the persisted head differs from what the client PUT, exactly like `seeded_pages`: refetch the draft canvas. WidgetKind.title: WidgetKind
WidgetKind.description:
Every inline interactive card the agent can attach to a block.

Wire values are frozen ``UPPER_SNAKE`` keys mirroring ``WIDGET_KIND`` in the
frontend's ``agent-chat.constants.js``; member names deliberately match them
so the two cannot drift. Every kind is declared even where no rendering
component exists yet — emitting an unbuilt kind is safe (the card renders
nothing and the block's prose still shows), but a *misspelled* kind is
indistinguishable from that, which is why nothing may build one by hand.

The mapping from this project's design catalog names (``resource_selection``
→ ``DATA_FINDER``, ``connector_validation`` → ``CONNECTOR_VALIDATE``, …)
lives in the initiative's contract-reconciliation document, not here.

examples.summary: whether to start now or later

TRUNCATE.description: Date truncation unit for date/datetime columns (e.g. 'DAY', 'MONTH', 'YEAR', 'AUTO').

INTERNAL_NAME.description: Internal name for the grouped column in the result.

COLUMN.description: Internal name of the column to group by.

draft_mode_schema_PipelineDraftMode.title: PipelineDraftMode
draft_mode_schema_PipelineDraftMode.description: Current draft mode status of the dataview

sequence.description: Version sequence the transcript was read from

history_index.description: The server-owned edit-timeline pointer (round-26): the index among the transcript's `changed` rows that the live canvas sits at. Every undo/redo/revert affordance is a pure function of the rows + this pointer, so a reload is byte-identical to the live session. null for a legacy transcript with no `changed` turn.

revisions.description: Every draft version, oldest first, with when it was saved and by whom — the history panel's author + time line.

features.title: Features
features.description: List of features in the segment

status.title: Status
status.description: Status of the workspace saying if enabled for the segment

split_segments_schema_OpValues.title: OpValues
split_segments_schema_OpValues.description: Operation to be performed on the segment

plan_create.description: Optional plan payload to create a new plan and switch the workspace subscription to it.

plan_update.description: Optional plan update payload to modify an existing plan. If plan_id is provided, that plan will be updated.

plan_id.title: Workspace plan ID
plan_id.description: ID of the plan assigned to the workspace

storage_gb.title: Workspace storage allocation
storage_gb.description: Chosen TOTAL storage allocation in GB on the plan

checkout_url.title: Stripe Checkout URL
checkout_url.description: Present when the plan change requires payment. The FE should redirect the user here to complete checkout.

next_action.title: Next action
next_action.description: BE-decided next step for the FE after the plan change (none / checkout_required / contact_sales / ...).

next_action_message.title: Next action message
next_action_message.description: Human-readable one-liner for the next action.

next_action_url.title: Next action URL
next_action_url.description: URL the FE should redirect to for the next action (mirrors checkout_url when the action is checkout).

bearerAuth.description: Primary credential. Authorization: Bearer mm_<token>. The token is issued server-side and shown once at creation.

workspaceId.description: Required with X-API-KEY and X-API-SECRET. Deprecated with them — use bearerAuth.
